title: Conformational changes induced in ubiquitin by circular protein-DNA chimeras
authors: Soumendu Boral; Michael D. Schnebly; Darartu M. Gamada; Kevin H. Gardner; Doeke R. Hekstra
one_liner_zh: 该文通过NMR研究环状蛋白-DNA嵌合体对泛素构象变化的影响，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作和结构方法，但非TF-DNA体系且无AI/物理模拟建模，仅部分相关。
abstract: Proteins are dynamic molecular machines that change shape in response to physical and chemical perturbations. Although single-molecule force spectroscopy provides precise information about the stretching of proteins in response to tunable forces, it does so without structural detail. Circular protein-DNA chimeras, with DNA attached to pairs of surface sites, have been introduced as an alternative way to tunably apply forces to proteins. Intriguingly, these chimeras should be tractable for atomic-level study by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and other structural methods. Here, we describe the NMR-scale synthesis of circular chimeras of single-and double-stranded DNA with ubiquitin, an essential component of many cellular pathways. We designed these chimeras to probe a two-residue retraction of ubiquitin’s C-terminal β5 strand, normally triggered by phosphorylation of serine 65 during initiation of mitophagy. We probed the resulting conformational changes by NMR and found that the attachment of a single strand of DNA suffices to alter this conformational equilibrium. A control bearing two separate short single DNA strands recapitulated much of the circular chimera’s NMR properties, supporting a dominant role for local protein-DNA interactions rather than spring-like action by single- or double-stranded DNA. These results provide a necessary benchmark for future studies using DNA springs to probe the functional dynamics of proteins. Significance statement Ligands, post-translational modifications, and mechanical inputs reshape proteins through forces that propagate across their structures. The underlying mechanical properties of proteins mediating these changes are rarely accessible with atomic-level detail. By producing NMR-scale circular protein-DNA chimeras, we provide a route to examining how defined physical perturbations alter protein conformational land-scapes. The results establish both the promise of this strategy and the need to account for local DNA-protein interactions.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质是动态的分子机器，其形状会响应物理和化学扰动而改变。尽管单分子力谱能够提供关于蛋白质在可调力作用下拉伸的精确信息，但缺乏结构细节。环状蛋白质-DNA嵌合体，其中DNA附着于成对的表面位点，已被引入作为对蛋白质施加可调力的替代方法。有趣的是，这些嵌合体应可通过核磁共振（NMR）波谱及其他结构方法进行原子级研究。在此，我们描述了单链和双链DNA与泛素（ubiquitin，多种细胞通路中的关键组分）形成的环状嵌合体的NMR尺度合成。我们设计这些嵌合体以探测泛素C端β5链的两残基回缩，该过程通常在线粒体自噬启动期间由丝氨酸65磷酸化触发。我们通过NMR探测了由此产生的构象变化，发现单链DNA的附着足以改变这一构象平衡。一个携带两条独立短单链DNA的对照样本在很大程度上重现了环状嵌合体的NMR特性，支持局部蛋白质-DNA相互作用的主导作用，而非单链或双链DNA的弹簧样行为。这些结果为未来使用DNA弹簧探测蛋白质功能动力学的研究提供了必要的基准。意义声明：配体、翻译后修饰和机械输入通过在其结构中传播的力重塑蛋白质。介导这些变化的蛋白质潜在机械特性很少能以原子级细节获得。通过制备NMR尺度的环状蛋白质-DNA嵌合体，我们提供了一条途径来检查明确的物理扰动如何改变蛋白质构象景观。结果既确立了该策略的前景，也强调了考虑局部DNA-蛋白质相互作用的必要性。
